<div class="clt-lesson batch-lesson" data-lesson="methods"><h2 id="learning-goals">What are we trying to understand?</h2><p><strong>How do the research question, variables, and design determine an appropriate analysis?</strong></p><p>A researcher should choose an analysis based on what the study is designed to answer, not which test produces the smallest p-value. Work through examples from the same attention-score and workshop contexts used throughout the course.</p><div class="clt-overview"><strong>Learning goals</strong><ol><li>Identify the research goal and outcome type.</li><li>Distinguish independent groups from paired observations.</li><li>Choose an estimation or testing method and justify it.</li><li>Identify assumptions and limitations before interpreting results.</li></ol></div><h2 id="explore">Make a prediction and explore</h2><section class="clt-simulator"><h3>Analysis decision guide</h3><div class="formula"><strong>1. What is the goal?</strong> Estimate, compare groups, describe association, or predict?<br><strong>2. What is the outcome?</strong> Quantitative or categorical?<br><strong>3. What is the design?</strong> One sample, independent groups, paired observations, or two measured variables?<br><strong>4. Are model assumptions and data quality adequate?</strong> If not, revise the analysis plan and explain why.</div><table class="data-table"><caption>Method families</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Goal</th><th scope="col">Possible method</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Estimate a mean</th><td>Confidence interval</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Compare one or two means</th><td>One-sample, Welch, or paired t-test</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Compare several means</th><td>One-way ANOVA</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Analyze categorical counts</th><td>Chi-square</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Quantitative association or prediction</th><td>Correlation or regression</td></tr></tbody></table><h3>Practice selecting a method</h3><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="0" data-why="One quantitative outcome from one sample is compared with a fixed reference. Use a one-sample t-test when assumptions fit."><legend>Is average attention score different from the established reference of 50? One group of 30 students.</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice0" value="0"> One-sample t-test</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice0" value="1"> Paired t-test</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice0" value="2"> Chi-square independence</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="1" data-why="The groups are independent and the outcome is quantitative; Welch compares means without requiring equal variances."><legend>Compare average scores for two independently recruited study groups.</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice1" value="0"> Paired t-test</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice1" value="1"> Welch independent-samples t-test</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice1" value="2"> Pearson correlation</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="1" data-why="The paired t-test uses within-person differences. Preserve actual matching."><legend>The same students complete a test before and after a workshop.</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice2" value="0"> Independent-samples t-test</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice2" value="1"> Paired t-test</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice2" value="2"> Chi-square goodness of fit</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="0" data-why="One-way ANOVA tests an omnibus difference among group means under its assumptions. Follow-up comparisons require a plan."><legend>Compare average scores among three independent instructional conditions.</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice3" value="0"> One-way ANOVA</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice3" value="1"> Three unadjusted t-tests</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice3" value="2"> Simple linear regression with time</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="0" data-why="A contingency table represents two categorical variables; check expected counts and independent observations."><legend>Do attendance status and criterion status (both categorical) appear associated?</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice4" value="0"> Chi-square independence</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice4" value="1"> One-sample t-test</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice4" value="2"> Pearson r on arbitrary codes</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="1" data-why="One categorical variable is compared with a fully specified null distribution."><legend>Does the distribution of three service preferences match prespecified proportions?</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice5" value="0"> ANOVA</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice5" value="1"> Chi-square goodness of fit</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="qpractice5" value="2"> Paired t-test</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset></section><h2 id="interpret">Interpret what you find</h2><ol><li>For each example, write the outcome, predictor/group variable, and whether observations are independent or paired.</li><li>State the quantity or population feature you want to estimate before choosing the test.</li><li>Identify one assumption that could change the method choice.</li><li>For your project, draft an analysis plan and a reasonable sensitivity analysis.</li></ol><h2 id="explanation">What is the method telling us?</h2><p>Method selection is not a lookup based only on the number of groups. For example, a comparison of means differs from a comparison of proportions; a prediction question differs from an association question. The methods listed are suitable only under their stated conditions. Complex designs, clustered data, missing values or multiple outcomes may require more advanced methods.</p><p>For a project report, describe the research question, variable definitions, sampling and design, descriptive statistics, chosen method and assumptions, estimates with uncertainty, effect size and limitations.</p><h2 id="knowledge-check">Check your understanding</h2><p>Choose an answer, then check your reasoning. Responses stay in your browser.</p><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="1" data-why="Both variables are quantitative; correlation describes linear association."><legend>Describe direction and strength of a linear relationship between study hours and attention scores.</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q0" value="0"> Chi-square goodness of fit</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q0" value="1"> Pearson correlation</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q0" value="2"> One-way ANOVA</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="0" data-why="Regression fits a directional prediction model. Check residuals and avoid ungrounded extrapolation."><legend>Predict attention score from study hours.</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="0"> Simple linear regression</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="1"> Chi-square independence</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q1" value="2"> Paired t-test</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="0" data-why="The research goal is estimation. Use a t-based interval when population SD is unknown and model conditions fit."><legend>Estimate the population average attention score with uncertainty, not test a reference.</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="0"> A confidence interval for the mean</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="1"> Chi-square test</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q2" value="2"> Correlation</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><fieldset class="clt-question" data-question data-correct="1" data-why="A rank-based analysis may be suitable for a distributional question. It does not automatically test equal medians."><legend>Compare two very skewed independent samples when the substantive question concerns a shift in distributions.</legend><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="0"> Automatically remove the largest score</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="1"> Consider a rank-based method with appropriate assumptions</label><label class="clt-choice"><input type="radio" name="q3" value="2"> Paired t-test regardless of design</label><button class="clt-btn clt-secondary" type="button">Check answer</button><p class="clt-feedback" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p></fieldset><p class="note">Textbook connection: OpenStax Introductory Statistics 2e, Chapters 8–13; integrated review.</p></div>
